key_insight: Experiments reveal a center-mode elastic instability at vanishing inertia in confined viscoelastic Kolmogorov flow, extending purely elastic instability to a rectilinear base flow.
engineering_relevance: This instability offers a potential route to enhanced mixing in low-inertia complex-fluid systems, including microfluidics, porous media, and polymer processing.
method: Drive confined quasi-two-dimensional viscoelastic Kolmogorov flow using electromagnetic forcing.
Observe velocity-field structures and fluctuations as forcing strength increases.
Use Oldroyd-B simulations to connect confined-flow dynamics to traveling arrowheads in unbounded flow.
evidence_signal: Experiments show arrow-shaped velocity structures and increasingly chaotic fluctuations, reproduced in Oldroyd-B simulations.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify mixing gains or establish how broadly the findings transfer beyond the confined quasi-two-dimensional setup.
paper_title: Experimental Evidence of Elastic Instability in Viscoelastic Kolmogorov Flow
